# Frozen released audio observations

The reference is unchanged Mluva 1.6.0 at `5202477edfe4b5d8bacfa5b2e9fd6eadd9624f7f`. Development collectors import the checksum-verified archive outside the maintained Rust tree and compare each imported audio, PipeWire and volatile-staging module byte-for-byte with that commit. Both fixture files retain their source digests and Python runtime version. The collectors and raw logs remain ignored under the worktree's `tmp/`; native checks require no interpreter.

`released-audio.json` contains 50 PCM16 RMS cases, 49 WAV metadata dispositions, 77 exact mixing/error results, 99 device graphs, eight dictation subprocess traces, five Meeting traces and one live recovery-header observation. The recordings cover fragmented input, complete 100 ms streaming chunks, an odd final byte, callback failure, exit codes 0/1/SIGINT, failed captures, stderr decoding/whitespace and forced termination after the finalization deadline. Final WAV bytes, source provenance, warnings, duration, private file modes and fixed argument vectors are compared with the released outputs. The WAV corpus deliberately retains a malformed RIFF boundary that raises rather than returning false. Mixing crosses the 4,096-frame boundary, averages negative odd sums toward zero and preserves unpaired tails.

The live observation uses enough synthetic PCM to flush the reference runtime's buffered WAV writer while capture remains active. Its header declares the first 1,600-frame chunk; ordinary finalization declares the complete recording. The native regression originally failed with a zero-frame header. Checks now compare the released header during capture and after SIGKILL of an isolated durable-capture owner. This establishes the reference's partial recovery metadata; it does not claim every unfinished sample is recoverable.

`released-audio-privacy.json` adds two real reference SIGKILL observations, one for dictation and one for both Meeting sources. Native checks compare memory-backed staging, directory/file modes, an independent cleanup session, an empty janitor environment, removal without an app restart and absence of durable audio. Additional native checks cover a dead janitor, refused disk staging, malformed/incomplete readiness, idempotent cleanup, child reaping, existing destinations, nested links and anonymous stderr. Signals target only newly created, verified fixture process groups.

All endpoints are compiled Rust fixture peers using deterministic PCM or frozen WAV bytes; no PipeWire server, microphone, sink, desktop session, provider, credential or user content is accessed. The peer is development test tooling and must not be installed. `mluva-audio-cleanup` is the production native helper. Actual PipeWire device capture, preparation/session guards in the app, provider transports, UI integration, installation and whole-app performance remain pending. These 291 frozen observations and 19 meaningful native audio tests are component evidence, not complete application parity.
